# BetterBags
[![Discord BetterBags](https://discordapp.com/api/guilds/1063213796845428876/widget.png?style=banner2)](https://discord.gg/a6DQuK8hV7)

[![CurseForge BetterBags](https://img.shields.io/badge/CurseForge-BetterBags-F16436.svg?style=flat)](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/better-bags)
[![Wago BetterBags](https://img.shields.io/badge/Wago-BetterBags-C1272D.svg?style=flat)](https://addons.wago.io/addons/betterbags/versions?stability=stable)
[![Package and release](https://github.com/Cidan/BetterBags/actions/workflows/release.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Cidan/BetterBags/actions/workflows/release.yml)

![BetterBags Logo](https://i.imgur.com/AyITAAV.png)

BetterBags is a bag replacement addon for World of Warcraft, inspired by AdiBags.  
It has a fresh, clean look, updated to the 2026 World of Warcraft art style.

It currently includes most of the features of AdiBags and is being worked on daily.  
If you have any feedback, please let us know in the [Discord](https://discord.gg/a6DQuK8hV7).

BetterBags currently supports the following versions of World of Warcraft:  
Retail (including Midnight and the various WoW: Remix versions as they come out)  
Classic (Era, MoP Classic, SoD, BC Anniversary, etc.)

# Summary
- Items are organized into categories and displayed in a Section Grid.
- Optionally, categories are organized into groups/tabs.
- Support for bags, bank, reagent bank, and Warband bank.
- The bag and bank can be anchored to a location and grow in specified directions.
- Customizable categories that contain items with multiple sorting options that can be pinned and toggled.
- Search based categories where the items within the category are defined by a search function.
- Items within categories have multiple sorting and stacking options (stack all, stack non-stackable, don't stack different transmogs).
- Powerful recent items support with customizable duration (mark all new items as recent, flash all recent items).
- Right-click category header to move or vendor all items currently in the category.
- Comprehensive Search that allows you to find an item most properties of an item (`Type`, `Subtype`, `iLvl`, and many more).
- Multiple built-in themes (Default, Simple Dark, Slate, Dark, Parchment, and ElvUI and GW2 UI themes when those are installed, for the classic bags and for BetterBags Next), with a declarative theme API for creating more.
- Bags that size themselves to their items, or windows you resize by dragging their corner (Settings > Resizable Window).
- Profiles to allow easy swapping of layouts and categories between characters.
- Category import and export strings to easily share your categories between friends.
- Robust plugin system allows for custom categories, configurations for user fine-tuning and even localization.
- Integration support for [Pawn](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/pawn) (upgrade arrows) and [Simple Item Levels](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/simple-item-level) (item level coloring).

More additions are being added all the time.

# Features

## Bag & Bank View
BetterBags offers its users a powerful category-based view, which also carry over to the bank.  

### Section Grid
This view sorts your inventory into their own visually distinct categories, allowing you to categorize items at a basic level that is easier for humans to understand by grouping like items together. 

The Section Grid offers:
- Customizable columns and number of items per row.
- Categories can be sorted either alphabetically (top to bottom), size descending, or size ascending.
- Categories can be pinned to the top, enabled, disabled or hidden at will.
- Items within these categories can be sorted alphabetically and then by quality (or vice versa).
- Multiple stacking options for fine-tuning your own experience.
- Built-in categories are named after the item's type and, when turned on in the options, its subtype and expansion (for example `Armor - Plate - Classic`). A subtype named like its type is not repeated, so quest items read `Quest` rather than `Quest - Quest`.

[![Section Grid View in Retail.](https://i.imgur.com/JLlOHxR.png)](https://i.imgur.com/JLlOHxR.png)

*Section Grid View in Retail.*

### Navigation
Most options and other important information in BetterBags can be accessed by left-clicking on the bag button in the top-left corner of the bag (or bank) to open the menu. Hovering over the bag icon displays a list of mouse-clicks that can be done for various functions. Some of the important functions in the menu are described in the following sections. Any options not in the menu directly are instead in the options screen (access by choosing `Open Options Screen` in the menu or the slash command `/bb`).

[![Menu in Retail.](https://i.imgur.com/jpMjAcP.png)](https://i.imgur.com/jpMjAcP.png)

*Menu in Retail.*

### Help
The Settings Window includes a Help page with guides covering BetterBags features, settings, search syntax, and troubleshooting. Open the page by typing `/bb help` in chat or by selecting Help in the Settings Window sidebar; adding words after the command, such as `/bb help auto sell`, opens the page directly on the search results for those words.

Typing in the Help search box ranks matching articles as you type, highlighting matched words in result snippets and matching word prefixes, minor typos, run-together words, and common synonyms, while the sidebar lists every group and article for browsing. Searching from the Settings Window sidebar also lists matching guides under Help Articles alongside matching settings. Both the sidebar tree and search results filter articles by your active bag design and game client version, displaying only the guides that apply to your current setup.

### Show Bags
This temporary view allows you to see your bags and the items within them how they currently are. It also allows you to swap out which bags are equipped for both the backpack and the bank.

[![Show Bags in Retail.](https://i.imgur.com/4YAG0Rm.png)](https://i.imgur.com/4YAG0Rm.png)

*Show Bags in Retail.*

### Dropping Items Into Your Bags
You can drop an item anywhere on the bag or bank window, not just on an empty slot: drag it there and let go, or pick it up and left-click the window. This is the quickest way to unequip gear, by dragging it from your character panel onto your bags.
- The item goes into the first free slot of a bag made for it (a profession bag of its kind, the reagent bag for crafting reagents, the keyring for keys on Classic Era, The Burning Crusade Classic and WoW: Forever), otherwise into the first ordinary bag, starting with your backpack. It is never put in a special bag it doesn't fit.
- Dropping on the bank window stores the item in the bank type you are looking at (your character bank or the Warband bank), starting with the tab you have selected.
- An item you picked up from the same window goes back where it came from.
- If there is no room, you receive the usual "Inventory is full." message and the item stays on your cursor.
- Dropping on an item swaps with it as always, and holding Shift while dropping on a category name still adds the item to that category.
- Items dragged from a vendor (buying) are not placed this way; drop them on a slot.
- A refundable item dropped on the Warband bank stays on your cursor, because putting it in the Warband bank ends its refund. Drop it on a Warband bank slot if that is what you want.

### Bag Anchor
By default, the bag and bank will grow from the bottom-left corner. Extending both up and right depending on the number of items per row and number of columns.
A specific anchor can be turned on by left-clicking the bag icon in the top-left corner of the bag and bank. It will allow you to drag the anchor to a specific pixel and grow the bag from whichever corner the anchor is in. Selecting `Enable` will turn on the anchor. Selecting `Show` will allow you to manipulate the anchor and choose the location. `Manual Anchor` will allow you to choose which corner you want the bag to grow from. If you leave it on `Automatic`, the bag will grow away from the closest corner.  
You can also enable and show the anchors with the slash command `/bbanchor`. To hide the anchor (but keep it enabled), simply right-click anywhere in the blue anchor.

[![Bag Anchor in Retail.](https://i.imgur.com/USio26V.png)](https://i.imgur.com/USio26V.png)

*Bag Anchor in Retail.*

### Free Spaces
The default view for free spaces is to have them in 1 icon with a number showing how many free spaces you have in each type of container equipped. Regular bag slots are on the right and special containers (like Reagent Bags) are on the left.
If you would rather see all of the spaces with their own icon, there is a setting in the config window to display them in that manner. When free spaces are all shown, non-regular bag containers will have a border around them to denote what type of container they belong to (Green for Reagent Bag on Retail).

	

		

			[![Free Space Icons in Retail.](https://i.imgur.com/6nMUB3s.png)](https://i.imgur.com/6nMUB3s.png)

		

		

			[![Show All Free Spaces in Retail.](https://i.imgur.com/NdUYAaj.png)](https://i.imgur.com/NdUYAaj.pngg)

### Extra Glowy Item Buttons
If you would like more glow on the action buttons (more like what AdiBags had), there is a setting to turn on Extra Glowy Action Buttons in the options screen.

	

		

			

				[![Normal Icons in Retail.](https://i.imgur.com/JaWJ90x.png)](https://i.imgur.com/JaWJ90x.png)

			

			

				[![Extra Glowy Icons in Retail.](https://i.imgur.com/abtd1fn.png)](https://i.imgur.com/abtd1fn.pngg)

			

		

		

			

				Normal Icons in Retail.
			

			

				Extra Glowy Icons in Retail.
			

		

	

### Item Level Upgrade Arrow
Equipment in your bags that is an item level upgrade compared to the gear you are currently wearing will have a green upgrade arrow in the top corner of the item in your bags. This permits you to easily see which pieces of gear in your bags might be an upgrade, such as when you're leveling and your item level is rapidly increasing.

Gear for an empty equipment slot counts as an upgrade too. An item receives no arrow if your character can't use it, isn't high enough level for it, it isn't your armor type, or it has a primary stat (Strength, Agility, Intellect) that your current specialization doesn't use. While you hold a two-handed weapon, one-handers, shields and off-hands receive no arrow, and while you hold a one-hander, two-handed melee weapons receive none; a one-hander is compared with your off hand only if you can dual wield. For stat-weighted upgrades, choose Pawn as the upgrade provider.

[![Item Level Upgrade in Retail.](https://i.imgur.com/QGjlIYX.png)](https://i.imgur.com/QGjlIYX.png)

*Item Level Upgrade in Retail.*

### Show Currencies
Currencies can be tracked at the bottom of the bag window. Up to 7 currencies can be shown at a time and tracking them is as simple as clicking on the currencies in the `Currency` screen in the Settings and choosing `Show in Backpack`. Any currency that is highlighted is currently tracked. If you attempt to track more than 7 currencies, only the first 7 in the list will be shown at the bottom of the bag.

[![Currencies Options in Retail.](https://i.imgur.com/I8B0zn3.png)](https://i.imgur.com/I8B0zn3.png)

*Currencies Options in Retail.*

[![Tracked Currencies in Retail.](https://i.imgur.com/2HeRBue.png)](https://i.imgur.com/2HeRBue.png)

*Tracked Currencies in Retail.*

### Configure Categories
Categories have a few ways in which they can be configured. All categories can be pinned. Custom categories can be deleted.  
- Pinning categories (Drag to the `Pinned` section) will display them in the listed order at the top of the bags. Any categories that are not pinned will be automatically ordered based on the `Section Sorting` option chosen in config.
- Deleting a category (`Delete Category` button after selecting the category) will permanently delete the category. If a category is created by a plugin, the plugin might create the category again when reloading the game.

### Category Groups
Category Groups allow you to put different categories onto different tabs to minimize the space required for your bags and focus on the most important items in your bags. Just hit the green plus icon to create a new group, then drag any categories you want onto the tab at the bottom of your bags. The default "Backpack" tab is always first and includes all categories that haven't been moved into a different group. Other groups can be renamed and deleted.  
If you don't want to use groups, you can turn it off in the settings.

## Bank
### Bank Tabs
BetterBags displays the different types of bank as tabs along the bottom of the bank window. It also includes the option to purchase the Reagent Bank and any available Warband Bank tabs.  
Tabs include:
- Bank (Showing all base bank tabs as well as bank bags for older versions).
- Warband Bank Tabs 1-5 (Called `Warbank Tab` in BetterBags).

[![Bank Tabs in Retail.](https://i.imgur.com/sxbCWNT.png)](https://i.imgur.com/sxbCWNT.png)

*Bank Tabs in Retail.*

### Bank Bags
To purchase bank bag slots, turn on `Show Bags` and click on any red bag slot.

[![Purchasing Bank Bag Slots in Retail.](https://i.imgur.com/UTl2bDg.png)](https://i.imgur.com/UTl2bDg.png)

*Purchasing Bank Bag Slots in Retail.*

### Character Bank Tabs
To show Character Bank Tabs, turn on the option in the Bank Menu. This allows all of the Bank Tabs to become tabs on the bottom of the Bank, beside the Warbank Tabs. When the tabs are shown, they work the same as Warbank Tabs described below.

[![Showing Character Bank Tabs in Retail.](https://i.imgur.com/UdAJJAZ.png)](https://i.imgur.com/UdAJJAZ.png)

*Showing Character Bank Tabs in Retail.*

[![Character Bank Tabs and Warbank Tabs in Retail.](https://i.imgur.com/8zHRoGY.png)](https://i.imgur.com/8zHRoGY.png)

*Character Bank Tabs and Warbank Tabs in Retail.*

### Warbank Tabs
Warbank tabs can be renamed and certain item types can be assigned to them by right-clicking on the tab at the bottom of the bank. This opens the Blizzard prompt to make any changes. Depositing items into the Warbank tabs will deposit them using Blizzard's rules for depositting items into the Warbank.

[![Editing Warbank Tab in Retail.](https://i.imgur.com/98Hgf2I.png)](https://i.imgur.com/98Hgf2I.png)

*Editing Warbank Tab in Retail.*

To deposit or withdraw gold from the Warbank, hover over the gold amount at the bottom of the bank/warbank window and left or right click. This works from any tab in the bank window.

[![Manipulating Warbank Money in Retail.](https://i.imgur.com/LQmRp1m.png)](https://i.imgur.com/LQmRp1m.png)

*Manipulating Warbank Money in Retail.*

## Recent Items
BetterBags places items that have been flagged as new by the WoW client in a special category at the top of your bag so that you can quickly find these looted items.  
**Note: To clear recent items manually, right-click the bag icon. On Cataclysm and Classic, you must install the [SortBags Addon](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/sortbags) to manually clear recent items.**

These can be further fine-tuned by:
- Setting a custom duration before they are sorted into their categories.
- Marking **all** items as recent (bank --> bag transfer, opening containers, etc.).
- Flashing new items in the stack to help the user find updated stacks more quickly.

[![Recent Items in Retail](https://i.imgur.com/svPb2eT.gif)](https://i.imgur.com/svPb2eT.gif)

*Recent Items in Retail.*

To disable recent items, uncheck the `Recent Items` category in the config window and set the `New Item Duration` to 0. After hovering over the item and changing anything in the bags, it will stop flashing.

## Move Categories
Right-clicking on a category header in your bank or bags will move the entire contents of the category to whatever other window you currently have open.
Supported windows include bags, all bank tabs, the mailbox, the trade window, and vendor windows. Selling items to vendors by right-clicking the header must be turned on in settings.

[![Move Category in Retail](https://i.imgur.com/b8BZTlX.gif)](https://i.imgur.com/b8BZTlX.gif)

*Move Category in Retail.*

## Search
BetterBags offers a comprehensive Search option that can be toggled with a keybinding (`BetterBags > Search Bags`).

When searching for bare words (eg. "Signet"), the search will match any item that has the word in the entire text of the default indices, which includes `name`, `type`, `subtype`, `category`, `equipmentLocation`, `binding`, and `tooltip`. A bare word that names a true or false field (eg. `collectable`, `toy`, `pet`) also matches the items where that field is true, so `not collectable` leaves out every pet you can still learn. Quote the word to search for its text alone. When searching in an index (eg. "name = Signet"), using the `=` operator will search in a prefix style, meaning the things you are searching for must start with what you type. To support full-text searching of each field, use the `%=` operator. The exception is `tooltip`: there, `=` and `!=` match the text anywhere in the tooltip, the same as `%=`.  
If you would like to exclude items in gear sets from your searches, the easiest way to do so is add `and not category = "gear:"` to the end of your search. (eg. `slot = finger or slot = neck and not (category = 'gear:')` will highlight all rings and necklaces that are NOT part of a gear set)
Search allows you to find items by the following indices (based on the item below):

[![Example Item in Retail.](https://i.imgur.com/Sc0JHZX.png)](https://i.imgur.com/Sc0JHZX.png)

*Example Item in Retail.*

### Strings
- `name` (name = "Tome of Unstable Power") The name of the item; the first line in the tooltip.
- `type` (type = Armor) The type of the item. Some examples include Armor, Weapon, Consumable, and Reagent.
- `subtype` (subtype = Miscellaneous) The subtype of the item. Some examples include Leather, Potion, Bag, and Bows. See the [Warcraft Wiki](https://warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/ItemType) for more information regarding type and subtype.
- `category` (category = "Gear: MW DPS") The category that the item is sorted into in BetterBags. In a search category's query, it is the category the item has without any search category (a custom category, a gear set, or its type), so a search category is never matched through its own name or another search category's. The one exception is a search category named after one of the item's equipment sets (`Gear: ` and the set's name): it replaces that set's category.
- `equipmentLocation` or `slot` (slot = Trinket) The item slot that the gear is for. Examples include Head, Legs, Main-Hand, and Finger.
- `expansion` or `exp` (expansion = DF) The expansion that the item is originally from. Shorthands are: Classic, BC, WotLK, Cata, MoP, WoD, Legion, BfA, SL, DF, TWW, Mid. `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` compare expansions in release order (`exp < legion` matches everything from before Legion), and an expansion can be given by its number (`exp = 3` for Cataclysm, 0 being Classic). In a comparison the start of a name works when only one expansion starts that way (`exp >= mid`, not `exp >= c`).
- `equipmentSet` (equipmentSet = "MW DPS") The equipment set(s) that a piece of gear is part of.
- `guid` (guid = 'item-60-0-4000000CAEA5CBE3') The globally unique identifier of the item. This string is unique to the specific instance of an item.
- `binding` (binding = soulbound) The text description of the binding type of the item. Possible values include nonbinding (items that do not bind), boe (bind on equip), bou (bind on use), quest (a soulbound quest item), soulbound (bound to a specific character), refundable (items that can be sold back to a vendor for a full refund), warbound (bound to a warband), bnet (bound to a battle.net account), or wue (warbound until equipped). **Note:** soulbound and warbound are only available on Retail because of API limitations on non-Retail versions.
- `tooltip` (tooltip = health) The full text of the item's tooltip. Unlike the other string fields, `=` and `!=` match the value anywhere in the tooltip, not only at the start.
- `bagname` or `bag` (bag = "Herb Satchel") The name of the bag the item is in: Backpack, the bag's own name, Keyring, Bank, Reagent Bank, a bank bag's name, or a guild bank tab's name. A plain search word does not search this field.
- `track` (track = hero) The upgrade track of upgradeable gear (Retail): Explorer, Adventurer, Veteran, Champion, Hero, Myth, in the game's language.
- `stat` (stat = haste) The stats on the item, by name: Haste, Critical Strike, Versatility, Mastery, Stamina, Strength, Agility, Intellect, Leech, Speed, Avoidance, sockets, and so on. `stat = crit` matches Critical Strike, as names match from their start.

### Numbers
- `level` or `ilvl` (ilvl = 528) The item level of the item. Non-gear items have item levels as well, but they are not shown to the user.
- `rarity` (rarity = epic or rarity = 4) The rarity of the item. Poor = 0, Common = 1, Uncommon = 2, Rare = 3, Epic = 4, Legendary = 5, Artifact = 6, Heirloom = 7.
- `quality` (quality >= 2) The crafting quality tier of a profession reagent or a crafted item, the number its quality icon shows (Retail only). Items without a tier have none, so `quality != 2` includes them. For Poor to Legendary, use `rarity`.
- `id` (id = 212685) The internal itemID of the item. A number uniquely identifying the base item. Specific ItemIDs can be found in the url on the item's WoWHead page.
- `stackCount` or `count` (stackCount = 1) The number of items in the stack for the item. **NOTE:** Currently count only checks the stack size of the "base" stack when using virtual stacks. For example, a virtual stack of 20, 20, and 3 to total 43 items will only be matched with either 20 or 3, not both.
- `class` (class = 4) The numeric representation of itemType.
- `subclass` (subclass = 0) The numeric representation of itemSubtype. See the [Warcraft Wiki](https://warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/ItemType) for more information regarding class and subclass.
- `bagid` (bagid = 2) The location of the bag containing the item. BagID is 0 for the main backpack, 1-4 for the bags, 5 for a reagent bag (Retail only), -1 for the main bank window, 5-10 (Classic) / 5-11 (MoP) / 6-11 (Retail) for bank bags, -1 for the bank (Classic/MoP), -2 for the keyring (Classic), -1 for the keyring (WoW: Forever), and 12-16 for warbank tabs. See the [Warcraft Wiki](https://warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/BagID) for specifics for each version of the game.
- `slotid` (slotid = 11) The slot that the item is in, in the bag that contains it. Numbered from 1 to N for each bagID, where N is the size of the container.
- `bindtype` (bindtype = 1) The binding type of the item returned by GetItemInfo(). 1 = BoP, 2 = BoE, 3 = BoU, 4 = Quest, 7 = BtA, 8 = BtW, 9 = WuE. See the [Warcraft Wiki](https://warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Enum.ItemBind) for specifics.
- `minlevel` (minlevel > 70) The character level required to use the item, 0 for none. Not the item level (that is `level`).
- `stacksize` (stacksize = 200) The most of the item one stack can contain. The size of a stack in your bags is `count`.
- `price` (price > 10000) The vendor sell price of one of the item, in copper (10000 is 1 gold). 0 for items a vendor will not buy.
- `maxlevel` (maxlevel >= 600) The item level of upgradeable gear once fully upgraded (Retail); for anything else, its item level.
- `upgradelevel`, `upgrademax` (upgradelevel = 3) How many upgrades upgradeable gear has, and how many its track has (Retail): an item shown as "Hero 3/6" has upgradelevel 3 and upgrademax 6.
- `petcount`, `petlimit` (petcount = 0) How many of a battle pet item's pet you have, and how many you may have (Retail).
- `slotequipped` (ilvl > slotequipped) For gear, the lowest item level you wear in its slots (both rings for a ring), 0 when you wear nothing there. A one-hander counts your off hand only if you can dual wield.
- `slotbest` (maxlevel >= slotbest) For gear, the best item level your character has had in its slot (Retail).
- `total` (total >= 100) How many of the item the bags contain altogether (the backpack's bags for the backpack, the bank's for the bank), counting every stack of it.

### Booleans
- `reagent` (reagent = false) Is the item classified as a reagent?
- `bound` (bound = true) Is the item bound to the character or warband? (From BetterBags internal module)
- `isbound` (isbound = true) Is the item bound to the character or account? (From Blizzard C_Item)
- `quest` (quest = false) Is the item for a non-active quest?
- `activeQuest` (activeQuest = false) Is the item for an active quest?
- `equipment` (equipment = true) Can the item be equipped (gear, and bags, which go in the bag slots)?
- `hasuse` (hasuse = true) Does the item have a Use: line in its tooltip, "Use: Teaches you..." on recipes and pets included?
- `cosmetic` (cosmetic = true) Is the item cosmetic gear (Retail)?
- `pet` (pet = true) Does the item teach a battle pet (Retail)?
- `upgradeable` (upgradeable = true) Is the item gear on an upgrade track (Retail)?
- `scrappable` (scrappable = true) Can the item be scrapped (Retail)?
- `inset` (inset = true) Is the item in any equipment set? (`equipmentSet` names one.)
- `upgrade` (upgrade = true) Does BetterBags show the upgrade arrow on the item? BetterBags uses the upgrade provider chosen in the settings (BetterBags, Pawn or SimpleItemLevel).
- `auctionable` or `ah` (auctionable = true) Can the item be posted on the Auction House? BetterBags queries the game, so the check covers bound and other items that cannot be listed. Classic Era and The Burning Crusade Classic have no such check, so there BetterBags evaluates the item directly: no for what is bound, a quest item, damaged, conjured, limited in duration or a wrapped gift, and yes otherwise, so the game may still reject an item with used charges or a lockbox. In the guild bank it matches nothing. `ah` on its own searches for those letters: write `ah = true`.
- `lootable` (lootable = true) Can the item be opened, such as a lockbox, clam or cache? Not in the guild bank.
- `usable` (usable = false) Can your character use the item? (Weapon and armor skills, level, professions, reputation: the red text in its tooltip.)
- `equippable` (equippable = true) Is the item gear your character can wear?
- `transmoggable` (transmoggable = true) Does the item have an appearance (Retail)?
- `collectable` (collectable = true) Is the item a battle pet you can still learn one more of (Retail)? Caged pets count.
- `appearance` (appearance = unknown) Is the item's look in your collection? `known` when any item that provides the same appearance has been collected, `unknown` when none has (Retail).
- `source` (source = unknown) Is this very item's appearance source in your collection? `known` or `unknown` (Retail).
- `toy` (toy = true) Is the item a toy? (Its tooltip contains "Toy".)
- `known` (known = true) Does the item's tooltip contain "Already known" (a toy, recipe, pet or mount you already have)?

The fields `quality`, `track`, `stat`, `minlevel`, `stacksize`, `price`, `maxlevel`, `upgradelevel`, `upgrademax`, `equipment`, `hasuse`, `cosmetic`, `pet`, `upgradeable`, `scrappable`, `toy`, `known`, `transmoggable`, `usable`, `equippable`, `auctionable`, `lootable` and `upgrade` are read once the game has sent the item's data, `petcount`, `petlimit` and `collectable` once your pet journal has loaded, and `appearance` and `source` once your appearance collection has loaded: an item that has just arrived may match none of them for a moment.

### Logical Operators
- `AND` (slot = Legs AND ilvl > 500 \[This will match leg pieces that are also greater than 500 ilvl.\]) The intersection of two terms. Items must match both sides of the AND.
- `OR` (slot = Legs OR ilvl > 500 \[This will match items that are leg pieces or are greater than 500 ilvl.\]) The union of two terms. Items can match either or both sides of the OR.
- `NOT` (NOT slot = Legs \[This will match any item that cannot be equipped in the leg slot.\]) The complement of a term. Items must not match the NOT. It works on its own, inside an `OR`, and before a group (`NOT (rarity = poor OR rarity = common)`).
- `(` and `)` To group search terms.
- **Precedence:** `NOT` applies first, then `AND`, then `OR`, as in most query languages: `type = armor OR type = weapon AND ilvl > 200` matches all armor, and weapons above item level 200. Use parentheses to group differently: `(type = armor OR type = weapon) AND ilvl > 200`. Rules saved before this precedence were rewritten once with parentheses, so they still mean what they meant.
- `=` (type = Armor, ilvl = 506) Items with a value equal to the text or number on the right side. This matches any items starting with the value.
- `%=` (slot %= Hand \[This will match any gear pieces that are slotted into any slot with `Hand` in the name. eg. Hands, Main Hand, Offhand\]) Items with the value in the full text of the field(s).
- `!=` (expansion != DF) Items with a value not equal to the text or number on the right side. This matches any items NOT starting with the value.
- `==` (name == "Hearthstone") Items whose whole value is the text (in any case), not just its start. With a number, the same as `=`.
- `~=` (name ~= "Hearthstone") Every item `==` does not match.
- `"` or `'` (slot = "Main Hand") To search for a multi-word string.

### Comparison Operators
**Note: These only work on numerical fields. Rarity names can be used with these operators.**
- `>` Items with a value greater than the number on the right side.
- `<` Items with a value less than the number on the right side.
- `>=` Items with a value greater than or equal to the number on the right side.
- `<=` Items with a value less than or equal to the number on the right side.

### Math, money and your character
Either side of a comparison can be worked out:
- `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` (ilvl <= player.level - 10) Arithmetic. Put spaces around the sign: `100-10` is still one word, as before.
- `min(...)`, `max(...)`, `floor(x)`, `ceil(x)`, `abs(x)` (maxlevel >= min(player.ilvl * 0.95, player.ilvl - 5)). `math.min` and the others work too.
- Money: `5g`, `50s`, `1g50s`, `20c` (price < 2g50s) are amounts in copper.
- Fields compared with fields, or with math on them (maxlevel > ilvl, price * count > 5g), are checked item by item.
- Your character: `player.level`, `player.ilvl` (your average item level, bags included), `player.equippedilvl` (what you wear), `player.class` (its name or its English token, `paladin`), `player.classid`, `player.spec`, `player.specid`, `player.profession` (any of your professions, by name or skill line: `player.profession = tailoring`), `player.name`, `player.realm`. A comparison of your character alone (player.level >= 80) matches every item or none, so `player.class = mage AND ...` limits a category to one class. Compared with an item's text, a value of your character is its value: `tooltip %= player.class` matches items whose tooltip names your class.

## Custom Categories
BetterBags allows items to be grouped into custom categories. These categories can be manually populated by the user, created by plugins, or created from a search.  
The title colour of the category can be chosen. Make a beautiful rainbow with all your categories!

### Manual Custom Categories
To manually create custom categories that you can add items to, left-click on an item, then hover over the bag button in the top-left of the bag, and left-click again. You can also left-click and drag the item to the bag button, then drop it. Enter in a name for the new category and your item will be added to it. To add new items into categories, you can do the same procedure with any category name, but hold shift while dropping the item.

### Ignored Items
On the Categories page, a category's **Ignored Items** tab lists items it never accepts, whatever would put them there: an item added to it by hand, a plugin's list, or its search. Drag an item onto the tab to ignore it, and right-click it to stop. An ignored item moves to the next category that matches it, or to its usual one. It works for a plugin's categories too.

### Gear Set Categories
Each equipment set you save in the Equipment Manager receives a category named `Gear: ` and the set's name, listed on the Categories page with your other categories. The category contains the set's items, and works like the other categories in the list: drag it up or down to set priority when an item fits more than one category, give it a color, choose which bags use it, hide it, ignore items, or give its items their own order. An item you add to one of your categories by hand stays there, even if it is in a gear set. If one of your categories, or a plugin's, already has a set's `Gear: ` name, the set receives no category of its own, and its items go to that category instead, which has priority by its place in the list. A new set's category starts at the top of the list, so set items stay in their sets until you move a category above one. Rename a set in the Equipment Manager and its category is renamed to match, retaining your settings; it can't be renamed in BetterBags, and items can't be added to it by hand. Delete a set and its settings are cleared, so a set you make later starts fresh. A gear set's settings are saved in your profile under the ID the game assigns to the set (assigned in the order you make sets), so characters sharing a profile share them: the first set your other character made uses the color and place you assigned to this character's first set. Give characters their own profiles to separate their gear sets. Nothing in an equipment set is ever sold, destroyed or deposited automatically. To turn gear set categories off in a bag, turn off its `Equipment Set` category setting.

### Search-based Custom Categories
Any search you complete has the option to be turned into a custom category. These categories will dynamically update as new items are added to the bag that match the search criteria.  
To create a Search Category, type in a search, then press `Enter`. Fill out the required information in the dialogue box and save.
- Category Name (string) is what the new category will be named.
- Search Query (string) is the search that will be run to determine which items will be in the category. Any search options (described above) will work in the query.
- The order of your categories determines which one receives an item that fits more than one: the higher one has priority. Drag them in the list on the Categories page to change it. A new category starts at the top, and an item you add to a category by hand stays there.
- Group By (string) allows you to create multiple categories from 1 string. Valid options are none, type, subtype, and expansion. This can be chosen as an option or included directly in the search string.  
`exp = mid and not "housing decor" group by type` will create a category for every type of item from the Midnight expansion, eg. "Midnight - Armor", "Midnight - Weapon", etc.

On the Categories page, a category's Search Rule box displays completion suggestions as you type: field names, operators accepted by a field, values present on your items, AND, and OR. Each suggestion displays how many results the rule matches once you take that suggestion. Press Up or Down to move through the suggestions, Tab or Enter to take a suggestion, and Escape to close the list.

### Automation
A category's automation applies automatically to its items. Pick the category on the Categories page (`/bb`), then its **Automation** tab:
- **Auto Sell**: when you open a merchant, the category's items in your backpack are sold.
- **Confirm Auto Sell** (on by default): with BetterBags Next's vendor window, the category's section is docked in the vendor window, glowing, as a category you drag onto the vendor is: double-click it to sell, right-click to put it back. Turned off, its items are sold as soon as you open the merchant. Hold Shift as you open the merchant to keep them. The classic bags have no such box, nor has BetterBags Next with **Enable Vendor Window** off: with it on, sell the category yourself by right-clicking its title.

Every sale, automatic or not, sells one item at a time, as fast as your connection allows (at least 0.2 seconds apart): selling everything at once causes the game to return "That object is busy." Anything a merchant won't buy stays in your bags, and isn't offered to that merchant again; it is offered to the next merchant that buys it. A merchant that buys nothing at all is sold nothing.
- **Destroy What Can't Be Sold** (requires Auto Sell on): the category's items no merchant buys are destroyed. With BetterBags Next's vendor window, its section is docked at the vendor like a sale, glowing red: each click destroys the next item, a whole stack. Anywhere, **Destroy Next Item** (Key Bindings > BetterBags) does the same. The game only permits an addon to destroy one item per key press or click.
- **Auto Deposit** (under Bank): when you open your bank, the category's items in your backpack go into it. **Deposit Into** selects your bank or the Warbank (retail); items the Warbank rejects, like soulbound ones, stay in your bags. Hold Shift as you open the bank to keep them. A category can sell at merchants and deposit at the bank at the same time.
- **Skip Recent Items** (under Recent Items, for any category, apart from the merchant settings): items assigned to the category skip Recent Items. They show in the category right away and are no longer marked new.

Automation never sells, destroys or deposits an item in an equipment set or a purchase you can still refund. Selling at once acts on a newly looted item by its category even while it shows under Recent Items; a section docked at the vendor contains only the items it displays, and a category that isn't on the backpack's current tab does not move to the vendor. A rule like `rarity = poor`, `ilvl < player.ilvl - 50 AND binding = soulbound` or `toy = true AND known = true` makes a category worth automating.

## Themes
BetterBags offers built-in themes, chosen in Settings > Theme: Default (Blizzard's look), Simple Dark, and Slate, Dark and Parchment, from BetterBags' sister addon Moonlight.  
BetterBags will detect if you have ElvUI or GW2 UI installed and offer an addon specific theme that matches your ElvUI or GW2 UI settings. BetterBags Next has its own ElvUI theme too: ElvUI's look in your ElvUI colors, textures and font, drawn again when you change them in ElvUI's options.

Themes are data: a theme describes how each kind of window and element looks, and BetterBags applies it to every bag, bank, dialog, panel, item button, tab, section title, search box and button. Addon authors can write their own; see [`sonata/README.md`](https://github.com/Cidan/BetterBags/blob/main/sonata/README.md).

Adds a searchable in-game Help to the settings window and fixes backpack items dimming at the guild bank.

## New

- **Searchable in-game Help in the settings window**: A new Help page in the settings window offers 80 searchable articles on everything BetterBags does, complete with links and the settings themselves. Open it with /bb help followed by optional search words, or find articles under Help Articles in settings search.

## Fixed

- **Backpack items no longer dim at the guild bank**: Backpack items are no longer dimmed while the guild bank is open. Previously, every item in your backpack, including tradable inks that the guild bank accepts, was greyed out during a guild bank visit.

Added an ElvUI theme for BetterBags Next, multi-tier and per-category item sorting, real-category gear sets, Gamepad UI support, and Warbank deposit improvements.

## New

- **ElvUI theme for BetterBags Next**: A new ElvUI theme for BetterBags Next uses ElvUI's art and follows your ElvUI colors, fonts, font sizes, bag text fonts, quest colors, icon crop, and Thin Borders outlines, updating live as you change ElvUI settings (Thin Borders needs a reload).
- **Multi-tier item sorting and new sort keys**: Each bag's Layout tab Order section now has Item Order, Then By, and And Then By dropdowns with sort options including Equipment Slot, Item Type, Expansion, Count, Sell Price (Stack), and Sell Price (Each). Existing saved sort orders migrate automatically.
- **Per-category item sorting**: The Categories settings page now includes an Item Order tab where you can enable Own Item Order and pick up to three sort tiers for any category. Per-category sort orders are also included when exporting and importing categories.
- **Upgrade Track item sort order** (Retail and WoW: Forever only): Added an Upgrade Track option to Item Order dropdowns that groups gear by its upgrade track, highest track first, then by current item level, instead of mixing tracks with overlapping item levels.
- **Gamepad UI support in bag windows** (WoW: Forever only): With Blizzard's Gamepad UI on, navigate backpack, bank, and Next vendor or guild bank windows with the d-pad, switch focus with triggers, use A, X, B, and the radial menu, and see button legends. Switch between mouse and gamepad anytime; focus and cursor position return after combat.
- **Dim backpack items refused by the guild bank** (Retail and WoW: Forever only): While the guild bank is open, backpack items that cannot be deposited into it are dimmed in both bag designs, matching how items refused by the Warbank or Auction House are shown.
- **Warbank deposit options in bank menu and settings**: When a Warbank is available, the classic bank's left-click menu now has Deposit All Warbound Items and Include tradeable reagents. Both designs also gain an Include Tradeable Reagents toggle in a new Warbank section on the Bank settings page's General tab.
- **Buyback tab flashes on vendor sales in Next**: Selling items while BetterBags Next's vendor panel is open now pulses the Buyback tab with your theme's glow so it is easier to spot where sold items can be recovered.

## Improved

- **Gear sets behave like regular categories**: Each Equipment Manager set is now a real category in your order, so manual categories and rules above it can take its items. Sets keep settings across renames, clear them when deleted, and support colors, Hide In, Used In, Ignored Items, and Own Item Order.
- **BetterBags Next vendor works with TradeSkillMaster**: BetterBags Next's vendor and TradeSkillMaster's vendor window now take turns instead of opening together. A new TradeSkillMaster button in Next's vendor header switches to TSM's window, and TSM's WoW UI button returns to Next's vendor.
- **Clearer side tabs in Default, Ember, and Quiet themes**: Unselected side tabs in BetterBags Next's Default, Ember, and Quiet themes now use a solid fill, a border edge, and higher-contrast text across all panels, with a highlighted border on the selected tab.
- **Sort Bank no longer deposits reagents**: Clicking Sort Bank in the classic bank now only sorts your bank items instead of silently depositing reagents into your character bank.

## Fixed

- **Deposit All Warbound Items warns before ending refunds**: Using Deposit All Warbound Items in either bag design now checks for refundable warbound items in your bags and asks for confirmation before depositing them and removing their refund timers.
- **Empty group hint clipped in classic bags**: The hint shown in an empty group's tab in classic bags is no longer clipped on the left or overlapping Free Space.
- **Papercraft margin note mirrored on left-side panels**: On BetterBags Next's Papercraft theme, the handwritten margin note on the bank, vendor, and guild bank panels now reads the right way round and sits at the same distance from the inner edge as on the backpack.
- **Specialized bag slot icons hidden on Papercraft**: Empty slot icons for reagent bags, quivers, and profession bags now tint using the theme's color so they are clearly visible on Papercraft's light paper slots instead of blending in.
- **Quest icons lingering on Classic bag slots** (Classic only): Theme quest icons and Masque quest marks on Classic item buttons no longer remain stuck on empty slots, subsequent items, or after switching to a theme without quest art.
- **Search maxlevel filter on upgrade track gear**: The maxlevel search keyword now finds the fully upgraded item level of upgrade-track gear instead of reading 0.

Adds a Food & Drink bar, bag anchors, Auto Deposit, per-interaction bag controls, single-category sharing, guild bank logs, and numerous fixes.

## New

- **Food and Drink bar for quick eating and drinking**: BetterBags Next now includes a floating Food & Drink bar (Settings \> Food & Drink) showing your highest or lowest item-level food and drink. Right-click a button to consume it, drag to move the bar, or drop it on the backpack to hide it.
- **Drop items on a bag title to assign a category**: In BetterBags Next, dropping an item on the backpack or bank title (or the bag button in Plain) opens a filterable category picker. Assign the item to any category, return it to its natural category, or create a new one on the spot.
- **Bag anchors and corner growth for small bags**: Small Next bags now grow from a held corner, and small backpack and bank bags gain an Anchor button (replacing Sort; right-click the title bar to sort). Click to show a 4-quadrant anchor square or lock the bag; dragging the title bar anchors to a bottom corner.
- **Log, Money Log, and Info tabs in the Next guild bank**: BetterBags Next's guild bank now includes Log, Money Log, and Info tabs at the bottom of its tab rail. Log entries display color-coded deposit, withdraw, and move icons, and authorized members can edit tab info text.
- **Auto Deposit items to Bank or Warbank by category**: Categories now have an Auto Deposit toggle and Deposit Into dropdown (Bank or Warbank, where available) under their Automation tab to deposit matching items when the bank opens. Hold Shift to skip depositing during a visit.
- **Choose bag behavior for each NPC and trade window**: General \> Interactions now offers a dropdown for each interaction (vendor, bank, mail, auction house, trade, and more) in both designs. Choose Open and Close (default), Open Only, or Leave Alone.
- **Export and import individual categories**: Your categories now have an Export button on the Categories page to share a single category. Importing one in Settings \> Profiles \> Import / Export lets you replace a matching category or keep both while keeping your own automation settings.
- **View and convert Blizzard categories in settings**: The Categories page now lists active Blizzard-built categories under Blizzard Categories with a Convert to Category button. Dropping an item on a Blizzard header or naming or renaming a category after one converts it too; converted categories cannot use Group By.
- **Hide Empty Groups option for backpack and bank**: A new Hide Empty Groups toggle on each bag's Layout tab under Tabs (off by default, both designs) hides tabs for empty groups. All group tabs reappear while dragging a section so you can still drop categories onto them.
- **Gap Between Sections layout toggle in BetterBags Next**: A new Gap Between Sections toggle on the Backpack, Bank, and Guild Bank Layout tabs under Sections (off by default) keeps one empty grid cell between side-by-side sections.
- **Sort items by Sell Price (Stack) and Sell Price (Each)**: Each bag's Item Order dropdown adds Sell Price (Stack) and Sell Price (Each), sorting items from highest vendor value to lowest with unsellable items placed last.
- **Show Mythic Keystone level on item buttons** (Retail only): Mythic Keystones now show their key level on item buttons, tinted by level when Show Item Level Color is enabled. Toggle this with Show Keystone Level under the Item Level section on the Backpack and Bank pages.
- **Toggles to disable Next vendor and guild bank windows**: Enable Vendor Window (Vendor \> General) and Enable Guild Bank Window (Guild Bank \> General) let you switch back to Blizzard's frames immediately without reloading. With the vendor window off, Auto Sell confirmations sell by right-clicking the category title.
- **Toggle to disable QuickFind integration**: A new Enable QuickFind Integration toggle under Integrations \> QuickFind (on by default) lets you turn the QuickFind item source and login message off immediately without reloading.

## Improved

- **Per-bag Size and General settings tabs, plus Vendor page**: Size settings (Icon Scale, Bag Scale, Autosize, Fit Names While Open) moved from Appearance to a Size tab on each bag's page, including a new Vendor page (with Autosize defaulting to off). Bank, Guild Bank, and Vendor enable toggles are now on each bag's General tab.
- **Compact export format and safer category imports**: Exporting categories now uses a compact format starting with !BB2!, and Settings \> Profiles \> Import / Export parses both new and older !BB strings strictly as data without running code.
- **Improved vendor quantity dialog with -, + and Max**: Shift-clicking a vendor item in BetterBags Next now opens a quantity dialog with -, + and Max buttons, pre-filled with one purchase's stack size and counting held currencies where supported. It no longer opens if you cannot afford any.
- **Plain theme full bags dock clear of screen edges**: In BetterBags Next's Plain theme, full-height docked bags now leave an 8-pixel margin at the top and bottom so frame artwork and the bag button no longer clip off the edge of the screen.
- **Plain bag button right-clicks to sort and adds menu items**: Right-clicking the bag button in BetterBags Next's Plain theme now sorts the backpack or bank (shown in its tooltip). Its menu also includes Sort and Small Bags across all panels.
- **Bag tab icons align neatly along the tab rail**: In BetterBags Next, icons on shown bag tabs now align in a single vertical column beside the panel edge instead of shifting horizontally with each tab's name.
- **Bags with slot gaps re-sort out-of-order items on close**: When Preserve Empty Slots as Gaps is enabled, closing a bag now re-sorts sections if newly looted items or growing stacks ended up out of order under the active Item Order.

## Fixed

Introduces dynamic bag autosizing, right-click backpack sorting, and the new Rainy Window glass theme for BetterBags Next.

## New

- **Autosize Bags setting for small bags**: A new Autosize Bags setting under Appearance \> Size automatically adjusts the height of small bags to fit their contents without scrolling while preserving your custom width. Bags smoothly expand and shrink as items are added or removed.
- **Right-click backpack title to sort**: Right-clicking the backpack title now sorts your bags, complete with sound effects and an updated tooltip hint. Left-clicking continues to chain panels together as before.
- **Rainy Window theme**: Adds the Rainy Window theme to BetterBags Next, turning bag frames into smoked glass with interactive lighting, condensation, and animated raindrops. New options in Appearance allow adjusting the glass tint and toggling rain, lightning, and opening sheen effects.

This update prevents text truncation in small Next panels and fixes an error when consuming items while bags are closed.

- **Text fitting for small panels**: Small BetterBags Next panels now widen just enough to keep bag titles and section headers from being cut off. A new Fit Names While Open setting under Appearance \> Size allows open panels to dynamically adjust their width as longer names appear.

- **Error when items are consumed with bags closed**: Fixed an issue where item recalculations caused an error if an item was consumed or cleared while bags were closed, such as when crafting at a trainer.
